title: Closer by degrees
summary: For people who barely know each other yet. Questions that go a little deeper each time, from a perfect day to what you'd regret leaving unsaid. Adapted from Arthur Aron's study of how closeness grows (1997).

content.welcomeNote: This gathering is for getting to know each other, a little at a time. The questions start light and go deeper as your circle settles in. Take them at your own pace, and say only what you'd like to.

welcomeQuestion.question: If you could have anyone in the world over for dinner, who would it be?

circles.name: Getting closer
circles.description: One question at a time, each a little deeper than the last.

questions.question: What would a perfect day be for you?
questions.context: Not a holiday, necessarily. A day you'd be glad to have again. From Arthur Aron's 36 questions (1997).

questions.question: If you could wake up tomorrow with one new quality or ability, what would it be?
questions.context: Pick one, or add your own. The circle will see what it wishes it had. After Arthur Aron's 36 questions (1997).

questions.question: What in your life do you feel most grateful for?
questions.context: Whatever comes first is fine. From Arthur Aron's 36 questions (1997).

questions.question: What do you suspect this circle has in common that nobody has said yet?
questions.context: A guess is enough. Sealed, so nobody's guess shapes the others. Recast from Arthur Aron's "three things you appear to have in common" (1997).

questions.question: What would you most regret not having told someone, and why haven't you told them yet?
questions.context: You don't have to say who. This is the deepest question here. Leave it for when your circle is ready. From Arthur Aron's 36 questions (1997).

openQuestions.question: How well do you feel you know the people in this gathering?
openQuestions.context: Just for now. It's worth asking again in a few weeks.
